messages:
oncall-bot: PAGE: SLO alert — streaming p99 tail latency > 2000ms in eu-west-1, auto-threshold triggered. Affected routes: /v1/streaming/generate (SSE). Currently ~37 active sessions with repeated stalls >5s. Paging oncall (priority: high). Details: https://redwood.inc/alerts/2065432100

sarah.j: ack. I'm on it. started a quick blast radius assessment — checking traffic concentration and recent deploys.

james.k: seeing a spike in proxy read buffers and long-lived write stalls. Metric snapshot: proxy_read_wait_count +420% in last 3m.

miguel: my suspicion — proxy is coalescing small chunks due to idle timeout + client RTT variance; when downstream client is slow we accumulate and then send a big chunk => perceived stall at p99. Also seeing elevated socket write queue in logs.

anya: trying a quick mitigation: I'll enable immediate_chunk_flush on the streaming-proxy config for eu-west-1 and reduce proxy.coalesce_window from 250ms -> 25ms. Will roll to 10% of proxy-pool first.

sarah.j: good. also will temporarily increase proxy workers in eu-west-1 by +30% and bump HTTP keepalive to 30s to reduce reconnect noise.

infra-bot: deploy: streaming-proxy config patch initiated by anya — rollout target: eu-west-1 proxies (10% -> 100% if stable). CI checks passed.

james.k: logs (snippet) showing stall pattern:
```
2026-03-14T14:12:03Z proxy eu-west-1 p-17 write_queue=342ms client_rtt=210ms coalesce_window=250ms chunk_size=0
2026-03-14T14:12:08Z proxy eu-west-1 p-17 write_queue=5100ms client_rtt=205ms coalesce_window=250ms chunk_size=12kb
2026-03-14T14:12:09Z runtime stream handler: stalled waiting on socket write for 4.9s (pid=8240)
```

miguel: that's classic slow-consumer amplification. Could also be a handful of misbehaving clients (large keep-alive but very slow reads). Any customer spikes?

ops-bot: customer-impact: 3 customers with heavy streaming usage in interval: [acme-payments, orb-analytics, beta-chat-prod]. acme-payments accounts for ~48% of active streaming sessions in eu-west-1. No explicit error rate increase yet, but degraded token delivery latency visible.

anya: the 10% rollout shows immediate drop in p99 for the proxied instances from ~3.2s -> ~0.9s. Rolling to 50% now.

sarah.j: great. I'm going to attach a rate limit at the edge for per-customer concurrent streaming sessions: temporary throttle 60 concurrent per-customer to protect cluster. Doing that now.

james.k: added an emergency firewall rule to drop long-idle clients (>60s idle) at the connection-proxy layer for eu-west-1. Should kill pathological slow readers.

infra-bot: update: streaming-proxy immediate_flush=true rolled to 50% in eu-west-1. Telemetry shows p95 improved, p99 trending down.

anya: small mitigation summary: immediate_chunk_flush + reduce coalesce_window + extra proxy workers + drop long-idle connections. These recoveries explain observed p99 drop.

miguel: we should also consider a longer-term change — make server-side write timeout configurable per-tenant and add a graceful fallback to chunked-heartbeat frames for clients advertising slow reads.

james.k: agreed. I'll open an RFC for per-tenant backpressure controls (rate limit + write-timeout) and a follow-up task to instrument per-connection socket write latency.

ops-bot: action items captured:
- sarah.j: keep edge throttle at 60 concurrent per-customer (temp).
- anya: finish rollout immediate_flush -> 100% and monitor 10m.
- james.k: open RFC + add socket write telemetry.
- miguel: prototype chunked-heartbeat frames.

sarah.j: handing off for overnight mitigation and follow-up to jessica (next oncall). Summary for handoff: incident started 14:12Z, p99 peaked ~3.8s. Root cause likely proxy coalescing + slow consumers in eu-west-1; mitigations applied reduced p99 to ~0.95s. Customer impact limited to streaming tail latency; no dropped streams observed after firewall rule. See logs and rollout links above.

jessica: acked — taking over rotation. I'll keep the edge throttle in place and monitor for 2 hours, then step down to 80 concurrent if stable. If p99 creeps back above 1.5s, I'll re-open pager and escalate to an incident.

oncall-bot: incident status changed to: mitigated (partial). Pager closed for current oncall. Continue monitoring.

sarah.j: quick postmortem notes: immediate cause = proxy coalescing behavior interacting with slow consumers; mitigation = immediate flush + coalesce_window reduction + drop idle connections + per-customer throttling. Next steps: RFC for tenant backpressure controls, per-connection telemetry, and client SDK guidance for streaming consumers to set appropriate read buffers.

jessica: copying notes into incident tracker and will schedule a short blameless postmortem sync tomorrow 09:30Z. Closing handoff.

oncall-bot: timeline entry: 14:12Z alert -> 14:16Z mitigation rollout started -> 14:24Z p99 recovered below 1.2s -> 14:36Z full mitigations applied -> 14:42Z handoff to next oncall.

sarah.j: thanks team. Please link RFC and CI test for immediate_flush behavior in the follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
